name: LegalBench
capability: Task-specific legal reasoning across classification, extraction, question answering, and generation.
construct: The suite operationalizes six lawyer-facing forms of legal reasoning through 162 independently authored tasks; it is a task collection, not a single latent legal-intelligence score.
size: 162 tasks; per-task instance counts vary
source: Expert-contributed tasks plus public legal datasets and authorities
input: Prompt plus task-specific facts, rules, clauses, or questions
output: Labels, spans, short answers, or generated text depending on task
metrics: Task-defined exact match / accuracy / F1 / generation scores: Each task supplies its own scorer; aggregate results must disclose task selection and averaging.
baselines: Paper evaluates 20 open and commercial LLMs; external Vals results are not the canonical paper leaderboard.
license: Repository/data licenses vary by contributed task
maintenance: Active collaborative repository; pin a commit because tasks and harness behavior can change.
reproducibility: Code, prompts, and public labels are available; cross-paper comparison requires the same task subset, prompt protocol, and model version.
risks: Public prompts and gold labels create direct contamination and overfitting risk. | Averaging heterogeneous tasks can hide severe failures in legally important sub-capabilities.
verified: Official paper and repository identify 162 tasks and six reasoning categories.
inference: The suite is best used diagnostically rather than as a single legal-intelligence rank.
ambiguities: Constituent task licenses are not uniform.

name: LexEval
capability: Chinese legal knowledge, inference, generation, discrimination, and ethics across 23 tasks.
construct: Six ability groups broaden evaluation beyond exams, but accuracy and ROUGE-L remain task proxies rather than a validated unidimensional legal-capability scale.
size: 14,150 questions across 23 tasks and six ability groups
splits: Evaluation collection; mostly multiple choice plus generation
source: Chinese legal exams, public datasets, authored and transformed tasks
input: Questions, facts, choices, or generation prompts
metrics: Accuracy: Exact option/label correctness for closed-form tasks. | ROUGE-L: Longest-common-subsequence overlap for generated answers.
baselines: Official paper evaluates general and legal-domain LLMs; the historical Collam site is not a stable leaderboard.
maintenance: Research release; claims of continuous updating are not a substitute for semantic versions.
reproducibility: Public prompts and data support reruns; pin task revision and generation decoding.
risks: Public exams and answers are highly contamination-prone. | ROUGE-L can reward surface overlap without legal validity.
verified: Official repository and paper define 14,150 questions and 23 tasks.
ambiguities: No stable current official leaderboard or project page was verified; the historical Collam hostname currently fails TLS validation.

name: ArabLegalEval
capability: Arabic legal knowledge, classification, question answering, and translation, with substantial Saudi-law coverage.
construct: The suite combines local and translated tasks; task scores therefore mix Arabic legal competence, general task performance, and translation artifacts.
jurisdictions: Saudi Arabia | Arab jurisdictions / translated sources
size: HF card exposes about 15.3k ArLegalBench rows, 11.6k MCQs, and 79 QA rows
source: Local legal material, translated benchmarks, and synthetic items
input: Arabic questions, text, choices, or translation prompts
metrics: Accuracy / F1 / ROUGE: Task-specific closed-form and overlap metrics. | LLM and human ratings: GPT-4-style judge scores for some generation plus human translation ratings; record the exact judge prompt/model.
baselines: Paper evaluates Arabic-capable and frontier LLMs across configurations.
license: No single clear unified code/data license located
maintenance: HF and GitHub artifacts exist; pin revision because configurations have evolved.
reproducibility: Mixed: public data, but judge/model versions and configuration counts require careful pinning.
risks: Synthetic GPT-4/Claude items and translated tasks can introduce generator artifacts. | The QA component is very small relative to the multiple-choice collection.
verified: Official organization GitHub/HF and paper establish the suite identity.
ambiguities: A unified release-wide license was not found.

name: ALARB
capability: Reason over Saudi commercial-law cases, complete arguments, and identify governing statutory articles.
construct: Verdict/argument generation is judged for correctness and partial correctness, while article selection uses MCQ accuracy; the protocol mixes open and closed-form constructs.
size: 13,344 cases linked to eight statutes; reported experiments use 1,329 cases and 1,159 MCQs per article task
splits: HF exposes a release without a clearly isolated hidden test
source: Saudi commercial cases and statutes, restructured with LLM assistance
input: Case facts/reasoning context or article question
metrics: Correct / partial / incorrect judge score: GPT-4o categorizes generated legal outputs against references. | MCQ accuracy: Exact statutory-article choice.
baselines: Paper evaluates multiple Arabic/general LLMs.
maintenance: Fixed research release; no canonical GitHub repository located.
reproducibility: Data are inspectable, but hosted-judge drift and absence of a hidden split limit strict reproduction.
risks: LLM-assisted restructuring and mapping can propagate annotation errors. | Public cases, labels, and references permit contamination and evaluation-set training.
verified: Paper and THIQAH-RD HF release identify the dataset.
ambiguities: No canonical GitHub or independent leaderboard was found.

name: ContractEval
capability: Evaluate long-context LLM clause-risk extraction on the public CUAD test set.
construct: F1/F2 and Jaccard trade off overlap precision and recall, while false-no-related-clause rate isolates abstention failures; the protocol reuses CUAD rather than defining new ground truth.
size: CUAD test set, about 4,182 QA rows over 41 categories
source: CUAD
input: Contract plus clause question
metrics: F1 / F2 / Jaccard: Overlap scores; F2 weights recall twice as strongly as precision. | False no-related-clause rate: Share of positive items incorrectly rejected as containing no relevant clause.
baselines: Paper evaluates 19 contemporary LLMs under one protocol.
license: No separate dataset; CUAD terms apply
maintenance: Paper protocol, not a separately maintained benchmark release.
reproducibility: Moderate if prompts/model versions are available; public API aliases can drift.
risks: It is not a new dataset and should not be counted as independent evidence from CUAD. | Paper figures use both 4,128 and 4,182, an unresolved count inconsistency.
verified: The protocol evaluates CUAD rather than releasing new labeled examples.
ambiguities: 4,128 versus 4,182 evaluation rows.

name: MSLR-Bench
capability: Extract structured facts and produce IRAC-style reasoning for Chinese insider-trading cases.
construct: Field-level extraction metrics test factual structure; IRAC recall and an LLM judge test whether generated analysis covers expected legal reasoning components.
size: 1,389 cases from 2005–2024 with 59,771 fields
splits: HF visibly exposes one train split
source: Public Chinese insider-trading enforcement/case materials
input: Case documents
output: Structured JSON fields and free-text IRAC analysis
metrics: Field accuracy / FCR: Exact or normalized field correctness plus the paper's field-completion/consistency measure. | IRAC Recall and judge score: Recall of expected IRAC elements plus LLM evaluation of generated reasoning.
baselines: Official paper compares general and legal LLMs; headline percentages must be tied to a named metric.
license: GitHub Apache-2.0 versus HF MIT metadata conflict
reproducibility: Public artifacts exist, but split isolation, license metadata, and judge version require resolution.
risks: One visible split allows accidental train/evaluation overlap. | Public cases and a single LLM judge create contamination and evaluator-bias risk.
verified: Official GitHub/HF/paper agree on the case/field scale.
ambiguities: Repository and HF licenses conflict; no hidden held-out split was verified.

name: MASLegalBench
capability: Multi-agent deductive reasoning about GDPR enforcement facts, rules, application, common sense, and conclusions.
construct: Accuracy measures final MCQ correctness; retrieval-at-k tests evidence acquisition; refusal and agreement statistics diagnose coordination rather than legal validity directly.
size: 950 MCQs from 15 UK enforcement reports: 647 yes/no and 303 four-choice
source: Fifteen UK regulatory enforcement reports; questions generated with DeepSeek and reviewed
input: Question plus retrievable report chunks
metrics: Accuracy / refusal rate: Exact final answer correctness and share of non-answers. | Retrieval@1/3/5 and Cohen's kappa: Evidence-hit rates plus agent/human agreement statistics.
baselines: Paper compares single- and multi-agent configurations.
reproducibility: Prompts/code are public; hosted models and multi-agent stochasticity need repeated trials.
risks: Only 15 source reports sharply limit source diversity. | Generator-authored questions can encode DeepSeek artifacts and source overlap.
verified: Official paper/repository define 950 questions and the 647/303 split.

name: LegalEval-Q
capability: Predict the quality of Chinese LLM-generated legal answers.
construct: A learned five-dimension regressor and adjusted aggregate score approximate human quality labels; it evaluates outputs, not legal tasks against authoritative answers.
size: About 10k source queries; 946 annotated items, about 9,460 model-output annotations, and 60 validation items
source: Legal queries, model responses, and AI-assisted/human quality annotations
input: Question and generated legal answer
output: Five dimension scores and adjusted aggregate
metrics: Dimension regression / AdjScore: Predict per-dimension quality labels and combine them with the paper's adjustment formula.
baselines: Paper compares evaluator models and correlation/agreement with annotations.
gating: Some model artifacts may require external platform access
reproducibility: Limited by licensing, model artifacts, and the small validation set.
risks: Training an evaluator on AI-assisted annotations can create circular model-family bias. | A high evaluator score is not independent proof that an answer is legally correct.
verified: Official paper/repository define it as an answer-quality evaluator.
ambiguities: Public license and complete artifact accessibility remain unresolved.

name: LRAGE
capability: Configure legal RAG evaluations across retrievers, rerankers, agents, judges, and custom corpora.
construct: LRAGE supplies orchestration rather than one fixed construct; validity is inherited from the selected corpus, task, judge, and metric configuration.
size: No fixed dataset
splits: Uses LegalBench, LawBench, KBL, Pile-of-Law, PLAT, bar-exam QA, housing QA, or custom JSON
source: User-selected public/custom corpora
input: Configured corpus, queries, and pipeline
output: Retrieval, reranking, answer, and optional judge results
metrics: Inherited task/retrieval/judge metrics: Metric set is configuration-dependent and must be reported with corpus and judge versions.
baselines: Paper demonstrates multiple legal RAG configurations; there is no one unified leaderboard.
license: MIT framework; selected corpus licenses vary
reproducibility: Potentially strong with a frozen config and dependencies; weak when users omit judge/model/corpus revisions.
risks: Cross-run comparisons are invalid when configurations differ. | It inherits every selected corpus's leakage, rights, and temporal-validity risks.
verified: Official paper/repository describe a configurable framework rather than a fixed benchmark.

name: prinzbench
capability: Answer obscure US legal-research and general information-search questions.
construct: Single-author human pass/fail attempts to measure research usefulness, but withheld items and non-blind grading prevent independent construct validation.
size: 33 withheld questions: 25 legal research and 8 search; three runs each (99 evaluations)
source: Author-created withheld questions
input: Free-form research question
metrics: Human pass/fail and pass@1: Author judges each answer; subtotals by legal/search category.
baselines: Repository reports selected model results; outsiders cannot rerun the same questions.
reproducibility: Not independently reproducible.
risks: Hidden questions reduce contamination but also block auditability and independent scoring. | Single-author non-blind judgments may reflect unmeasured preferences.
verified: Public repository describes 33 private questions and 99 runs.
ambiguities: Question contents, rubric detail, and license are unavailable.

name: Open Legal-Answer Benchmark
capability: Produce current US legal answers with relevant, supported, and correctly ranged citations.
construct: Checklist and citation metrics separate substantive required points, forbidden claims, authority retrieval, and citation entailment/range instead of collapsing answer quality into one judge score.
size: 54 base questions (29 hard, 25 controls) plus 8 adversarial variants; 62 JSONL rows
source: Sponsor-authored current-law questions and cited authorities
input: Legal question
metrics: Must-include / must-not / authority retrieval: Rule/checklist scoring of required propositions, prohibited errors, and retrieval of the right authority. | Citation support and in-range: Check whether citations support the associated claim and point to the relevant passage; optional LLM judging is separate.
baselines: Sponsor-maintained self-runs are recorded in the repository leaderboard.
maintenance: Active sponsor-maintained benchmark; versioning matters for current-law questions.
reproducibility: Public data and scorer support reruns; browser/search availability and current sources can change outcomes.
risks: Fully public questions permit direct optimization. | Sponsor-run results are not an independent third-party audit.
verified: Official repository exposes the 62-row JSONL and leaderboard.
ambiguities: Temporal legal changes can make older gold expectations stale.

name: LawBench
capability: Chinese legal memorization, understanding, and application across 20 tasks.
construct: Tasks are arranged into memorization, understanding, and application levels, testing retrieval of legal knowledge separately from applying it to cases and generated outputs.
size: 10,000 examples: 20 tasks × 500
splits: Evaluation-oriented task files; no unified hidden split
source: Chinese exams and public legal NLP datasets including CAIL/JEC-QA/LAIC sources
input: Task-specific JSON text, questions, facts, or documents
output: Choices, labels, extracted items, numeric values, or generated text
metrics: Official 20-task metric map: 1-1 ROUGE-L; 1-2 accuracy; 2-1 F0.5; 2-2 F1; 2-3 F1; 2-4 accuracy; 2-5 character-level rc-F1; 2-6 entity soft-F1; 2-7 ROUGE-L; 2-8 accuracy; 2-9 F1; 2-10 trigger soft-F1; 3-1 F1; 3-2 ROUGE-L; 3-3 F1; 3-4 and 3-5 normalized log-distance; 3-6 accuracy; 3-7 accuracy; 3-8 ROUGE-L. Report per-task scores because the official AVG mixes unlike scales. | Normalized log-distance (3-4/3-5): For scorable prison-term items, score = 1 - mean(|ln(gold_months+1)-ln(pred_months+1)|)/ln(216). The evaluator uses the first parsed month value, otherwise the first year value multiplied by 12; an unparsed prediction receives distance ln(216). Gold death/life-imprisonment rows are skipped. | Abstention rate: The evaluator separately reports the fraction of rows whose answer parser cannot extract a valid task-specific response. This is not folded consistently into every task score, and the 2-6 evaluator misspells its returned abstention key, so the top-level CSV records zero for that task unless corrected.
baselines: Official paper compares general and legal-domain LLMs; OpenCompass hosts results.
dataset_access: Public GitHub release; linked HF copy is third-party
license: Repository license applies to code; source-dataset terms vary
maintenance: Repository is available; use a pinned revision.
reproducibility: Prompts and evaluator code are public, but there is no canonical author-owned HF dataset and source tasks have mixed provenance. Pin and inspect the scorer: parsing rules, skipped rows, and abstention handling affect the result.
risks: Public exam and CAIL-derived answers create high contamination risk. | The headline AVG arithmetically mixes heterogeneous task metrics, while task-specific parsers and inconsistent abstention handling can change scores. | A third-party HF mirror can drift from the canonical repository.
verified: Official repository defines 20 tasks with 500 samples per task. | Official README and evaluator code define the task-to-metric map, normalized log-distance, and parser-based abstention reporting.
inference: Per-task reporting is more interpretable than the heterogeneous official AVG.
ambiguities: No official canonical HF release was located. | The official 2-6 evaluator returns the misspelled key 'anstention_rate', so the top-level evaluator silently writes zero abstention for that task.

name: Massive Legal Embedding Benchmark
capability: Legal embedding quality across retrieval, retrieval-augmented QA, and zero-shot classification tasks.
construct: MTEB-compatible task configurations treat rank quality—usually nDCG@10—as the main proxy for useful legal representations, supplemented by QA and classification task scores.
jurisdictions: United States | United Kingdom | European Union | Australia | Ireland | Singapore
size: 10 constituent datasets
source: Public legal retrieval, QA, and classification datasets assembled by Isaacus
input: Queries and candidate texts or labeled examples
output: Ranked candidates, answers, or zero-shot labels
metrics: nDCG@10: Discounted graded gain at rank 10, normalized by the ideal ranking; constituent tasks may add QA/classification metrics.
baselines: Public result files and an Isaacus-hosted leaderboard compare general and legal embedding models.
license: MIT code; constituent dataset licenses vary
maintenance: Active vendor-maintained suite; pin task configs and result commit.
reproducibility: Evaluator is public and MTEB-compatible; API embeddings and changing hosted model aliases can still move scores.
risks: All public queries and labels permit benchmark-targeted optimization. | Benchmark owner also sells a leading model, so independently reproduced results are preferable.
verified: Both source README bullets resolve to the same GitHub repository and benchmark identity.
ambiguities: The original awesome-list Kanon/MLEB URL could not be verified as canonical.

name: Contract Understanding Atticus Dataset
capability: Locate 41 categories of commercially important clauses in long contracts.
construct: Extractive QA turns issue spotting into span retrieval: a model should find every relevant token while avoiding unrelated language and correctly abstain when a clause is absent.
size: 510 contracts; 13,000+ expert labels; common QA release has 22,450 train and 4,182 test rows
source: Material contracts filed in SEC EDGAR
input: Contract text plus a clause-category question
output: One or more answer spans, or no answer
metrics: Token intersection-over-union (Jaccard): |predicted-token set ∩ gold-token set| / |union|, with precision/recall and AUPR across confidence thresholds. | AUPR: Area under the precision–recall curve over clause predictions, useful under strong class imbalance.
baselines: Paper reports BERT-family extractive QA baselines; many later long-context systems reuse the public test set.
license: CC BY 4.0 for annotations/release; source contracts retain underlying rights
reproducibility: Data and evaluation code are public; normalize tokenization and no-answer handling exactly.
risks: Public contracts and gold spans are heavily reused and contamination-prone. | Boilerplate similarity can reward memorization more than issue spotting on novel drafting styles.
verified: Official project, GitHub, paper, and author HF release agree on the benchmark identity.
ambiguities: Published descriptions count annotations, QA rows, and labels differently; state which unit is reported.

name: LEDGAR
capability: Classify contract provisions into clause/topic labels.
construct: Provision classification measures whether representations separate contract-language topics; macro-F1 exposes rare-label performance while micro-F1 emphasizes the frequent-label mass.
size: Original corpus: about 846,274 provisions, 12,608 labels, 60,540 contracts; LexGLUE subset: 60k/10k/10k over 100 labels
source: SEC EDGAR contracts
input: A contract provision
metrics: Micro-F1 and macro-F1: Micro pools all label decisions; macro averages per-label F1 so rare labels have equal weight.
baselines: Original paper and LexGLUE report neural and transformer classifiers.
dataset_access: Public code/data paths; LexGLUE package is directly loadable
license: LexGLUE package CC BY 4.0; underlying filing rights and original release terms should be reviewed
maintenance: Original dataset is stable; LexGLUE is the maintained standardized task.
reproducibility: Strong if the exact original versus LexGLUE variant, label vocabulary, and split are named.
risks: SEC boilerplate enables document-family leakage and near-duplicate memorization. | Reporting LEDGAR without naming the original or 100-label LexGLUE variant is ambiguous.
verified: The README's Metatext link is secondary; the original repository and LexGLUE are canonical sources.
ambiguities: Source-rights treatment is not identical to the annotation license.

name: ECtHR Tasks A/B
capability: Predict European Convention articles alleged (Task A) or found violated (Task B) from case facts.
construct: Multi-label outcome prediction tests fact-to-doctrine mapping; macro-F1 emphasizes less frequent Convention articles and micro-F1 the total decision mass.
jurisdictions: European Court of Human Rights / Council of Europe
size: Roughly 11,000 cases per LexGLUE Task A/B configuration
source: Public ECtHR judgments and case facts
input: Case-fact section
metrics: Micro-F1 and macro-F1: F1 is computed over article labels with micro and label-macro aggregation.
baselines: Original Chalkidis et al. work and LexGLUE report transformer and long-document baselines.
dataset_access: Public LexGLUE configs ecthr_a and ecthr_b
maintenance: Stable LexGLUE release; the older coastalcph/ecthr_cases HF path is stale.
reproducibility: Good with the exact task config, long-document truncation strategy, and thresholding specified.
risks: Judgments and labels are public and likely represented in pretraining corpora. | Outcome labels can be learned from stylistic or temporal shortcuts rather than legal reasoning.
verified: LexGLUE is the current canonical distribution path.
ambiguities: Counts vary slightly across original and standardized releases.

name: awesome-legal-nlp
capability: Discovery index for legal NLP datasets, models, papers, surveys, books, and events.
construct: No evaluation construct is defined; this is a curated bibliography/resource list, not an instrument for measuring model capability.
size: No benchmark instances
source: Community-curated links
input: Not applicable
metrics: Not applicable: No scorer or evaluation protocol exists.
baselines: None.
reproducibility: Not applicable as an evaluation artifact.
risks: Treating a resource list as a benchmark confuses discovery coverage with measured capability.
verified: Repository contents are links and prose rather than instances, gold labels, or graders.

name: JUST-NLP 2025 Legal MT Shared Task
capability: Translate legal text from English to Hindi.
construct: Reference-based machine-translation metrics reward n-gram or character overlap; the shared task complements them with semantic metrics but still cannot alone establish legal fidelity.
size: InLMT: 50,000 train, 5,000 validation, 5,000 hidden test sentences
splits: Train/validation plus hidden Codabench test references
source: Indian legal parallel text released for the shared task
input: XLSX rows containing English legal sentences and IDs
output: CSV with ID and Hindi translation
metrics: AutoRank: Arithmetic mean of six 0–100 normalized metrics: BLEU, METEOR, inverted TER, chrF++, BERTScore, and COMET; each receives equal weight. | BLEU / METEOR / TER / chrF++ / BERTScore / COMET: Report all six component metrics; higher is better except raw TER, where lower is better. ROUGE scores appear in additional model analysis but are not part of AutoRank.
baselines: The findings paper's Table 2 ranks Team-SVNIT first at AutoRank 61.62; the abstract instead says the highest AutoRank was 72.1, an unresolved internal conflict.
license: Not clearly stated in the durable public materials
gating: Codabench account may be required for files/submission
maintenance: Completed 2025 shared task; not a continuously maintained benchmark.
reproducibility: Hidden references support clean competition scoring, but long-term artifact access and exact dependency versions are uncertain.
risks: Automatic overlap metrics can reward fluent mistranslations or penalize legally equivalent wording. | The original README linked stale Codabench competition 3682; 10351 is the verified competition.
verified: The official findings paper and competition materials define the 50k/5k/5k splits, six AutoRank components, normalization direction, and equal-weight aggregation.
ambiguities: A clear dataset license was not located. | The findings abstract reports a top AutoRank of 72.1 while Table 2 and the official result sheet report 61.62.

name: LegalBench-RAG
capability: Retrieve exact supporting spans from long legal and policy documents.
construct: Character-level precision and recall directly measure whether retrieved text covers gold support while limiting extra context; this isolates retrieval from answer generation.
jurisdictions: United States | mixed contracts and policies
size: 714 documents, more than 79M characters; 6,858 queries in abstract versus 6,889 in a paper table
source: Four public contract/policy datasets
input: Query plus document corpus
output: Document identifier and character start/end spans
metrics: Character precision and recall: Overlap between predicted and reference character sets, exposing both missed support and context bloat.
baselines: Paper evaluates retrieval systems at several context budgets.
license: MIT code; constituent source licenses vary
reproducibility: High for retrieval when the exact commit, corpus, character normalization, and context budget are pinned.
risks: No hidden split; queries, corpus, and spans are public. | The paper's query counts conflict and should never be silently harmonized.
verified: Official repository and paper define exact-span evaluation.
ambiguities: 6,858 versus 6,889 query count remains unresolved.

name: LegalAgentBench
capability: Chinese legal tool use, multi-hop information gathering, and legal writing.
construct: Success and progress scores estimate whether an agent selects and sequences tools toward a task; BERTScore assesses writing similarity, but neither alone proves legal correctness.
size: 17 corpora, 37 tools, 300 tasks
splits: Tasks span one-to-five-hop and writing categories
source: Chinese legal corpora wrapped as tools and authored tasks
input: Natural-language task plus tool environment
output: JSON tool calls and a final legal answer or document
metrics: Keyword success rate / progress rate: Rule-based matching of required milestones and final keywords across task trajectories. | BERTScore: Contextual token similarity for generated legal writing; token use is also reported.
baselines: Paper compares multiple LLM agents and prompting configurations.
dataset_access: Public code, data, prompts, and environment
gating: Model/API credentials may be needed to run baselines
reproducibility: Harness is public; API model drift and environment dependencies still affect trajectories.
risks: Keyword graders can be gamed without producing a legally adequate result. | Public solutions and tool corpora permit benchmark-specific planning.
verified: Official repository specifies 17 corpora, 37 tools, and 300 tasks.
inference: Use as a tool-use benchmark with legal grounding checks, not as proof of deployable lawyering.

name: LEXam
capability: Answer bilingual law-school multiple-choice and open-answer examination questions.
construct: MCQ accuracy measures answer selection; open-answer ensemble judging estimates substantive coverage against references, making judge version and rubric part of the instrument.
jurisdictions: Germany | United States / English-language courses | mixed law-school curricula
size: 7,537 questions from 340 exams and 116 courses: 2,841 open-answer and 4,696 MCQ
splits: Versioned JSON release; no single training split is required
source: University law examinations and course materials
input: Question, optional choices, and metadata
metrics: MCQ accuracy: Exact selected-option correctness. | Open-answer judge ensemble: Multiple LLM judges score generated answers against references; record judge model versions and aggregation.
baselines: Official results compare broad frontier/open models; project site tracks benchmark resources.
maintenance: Active versioned benchmark; item count changed from an earlier 4,886-item release.
reproducibility: Good when dataset revision, prompts, judge ensemble, and model endpoints are pinned.
risks: Public exams and answers are contamination-prone. | Open-answer rankings can move when hosted judges or ensemble membership changes.
verified: Official GitHub/HF/project sources agree on the current 7,537-question release.
ambiguities: Jurisdiction is course-dependent rather than a single national-law corpus.

name: LexGLUE
capability: Standardized English legal language understanding across seven classification and judgment tasks.
construct: LexGLUE standardizes task splits and reporting across ECtHR A/B, SCOTUS, EUR-LEX, LEDGAR, UNFAIR-ToS, and CaseHOLD; it measures a portfolio of NLU tasks rather than one jurisdiction-neutral ability.
jurisdictions: Council of Europe | European Union | United States | mixed contracts/terms
size: Seven constituent datasets
source: Previously released legal datasets normalized by the LexGLUE authors
input: Case facts, opinions, provisions, legislation, or terms of service
metrics: Macro-F1 and micro-F1 / task accuracy: Task-appropriate classification metrics; report each task and disclose any cross-task averaging.
baselines: Official repository reports BERT, RoBERTa, LegalBERT, hierarchical, Longformer, and BigBird baselines.
license: CC BY 4.0 package; constituent-source rights should still be checked
reproducibility: High when task config, long-document handling, thresholds, and aggregate convention are pinned.
risks: All constituent test labels are public and likely present in model-development workflows. | A single aggregate hides jurisdiction and task-family failures.
verified: Official GitHub/HF/paper define seven tasks and standardized splits.
inference: LexGLUE is a strong comparability suite, not a deployability claim.

name: Competition on Legal Information Extraction/Entailment
capability: Retrieve and recognize entailment among Canadian cases and Japanese civil-code provisions.
construct: Four annual tasks separate first-stage authority retrieval from textual entailment; official hidden tests reduce direct leakage, while task-specific precision/recall/F1 and accuracy measure different stages.
size: Annual task packages; counts change by year
splits: Released training data plus competition-held test labels
source: Canadian case law and Japanese civil-code/bar-exam materials
input: Query case or legal question with candidate cases/statutes
metrics: Precision / recall / F1: Official task scripts score retrieved cases/statutes and entailment selections; exact primary metric varies by task/year. | Accuracy: Used for binary statutory entailment/answer tasks where specified by the year's rules.
baselines: Annual proceedings and official results compare participating systems.
maintenance: Annual competition; never mix editions without naming the year.
reproducibility: Strong within an edition if official data/scripts are retained; no single canonical GitHub or HF release spans years.
risks: Task definitions, corpora, and metrics change between annual editions. | Competition access terms and later link rot can limit retrospective reproduction.
verified: Official COLIEE 2025 site defines four tasks and competition access.
ambiguities: There is intentionally no single edition-independent dataset size or metric.

name: Ready Jurist One
capability: Operate interactively in Chinese legal consultation, drafting, civil-court, and criminal-court environments.
construct: J1-EVAL uses dual outcome- and process-oriented scoring so an agent must reach the right result and follow required procedural steps, formats, reasoning, and citation constraints.
size: Paper reports 508 environments across six scenarios and three levels
source: Chinese judgments and legal articles, structured into role-based environments
input: Multi-turn role interactions, facts, and procedural state
output: Answers, complaints/defences, courtroom actions, reasons, citations, and judgments
metrics: Outcome-oriented scores: Binary/non-binary answer score, component document score, judgment score, crime accuracy, and normalized-log penalty deviation. | Process-oriented scores: Format following, procedural stage completeness, reasoning quality, and cited-law precision; except procedural completeness, metrics use explicit references.
baselines: Official paper evaluates 17 general, open, and legal-specific agents; OpenCompass integration is linked.
license: No clear repository license was visible in the primary GitHub page
gating: API models and significant compute may be required
reproducibility: Harness and data are public, but simulator/judge model drift and stochastic multi-agent interaction require repeated trials.
risks: LLM-driven roles and judges can create correlated simulator/evaluator bias. | The paper states 508 total but lists 160 + 186 + 192 = 538 level instances; this arithmetic conflict is unresolved.
verified: Official GitHub/project/paper define six scenarios and the dual metric table.
ambiguities: Reported total and per-level counts conflict; licensing is unclear.

name: Legal Agent Benchmark
capability: Complete long-horizon legal matters using files, research, analysis, drafting, and validation tools.
construct: All-pass treats legal work as conjunctive reliability: a task passes only if every required expert rubric criterion passes; rubric pass rate exposes partial completion but is not the headline autonomy threshold.
jurisdictions: United States / commercial legal practice | mixed practice areas
size: Evolving public release; launch materials describe 1,200+ tasks, 24 practice areas, and 75,000+ rubric criteria, with later contracting extensions
splits: Public task set plus Harvey's separate holdout used for published model results
source: Synthetic client matters and expert-curated instructions, files, outputs, and rubrics
input: Matter instruction and sandboxed document/file environment
output: Research, analysis, and professional work-product artifacts

name: APEX-Agents — Corporate Lawyer

name: DeonticBench

Numeric domains allow ±1 rounding tolerance; categorical domains require exact match. | Abstention and wrong rate: Empty/error/timeout Prolog or unparsable direct answer counts as abstention; remaining incorrect parses count wrong.

name: Korean Canonical Legal Benchmark

name: RedlineBench
capability: Negotiate commercial contracts over four turns by producing native Word tracked changes and comments.

name: SwiLTra-Bench
capability: Translate Swiss laws, court headnotes, and press releases among official Swiss languages and English.

source: Swiss laws, decision summaries/headnotes, and Supreme Court press releases

verified: Official paper/GitHub/HF collection define the corpus families and evaluator set.

name: Multilingual Indian Legal Parallel Corpus

name: Legal RAG Bench
capability: Evaluate an end-to-end legal RAG pipeline and attribute errors to retrieval versus generation.

name: CanLegalRAGBench
capability: Retrieve Canadian case law for realistic layperson and legal-professional queries and generate grounded answers.

name: LEXTREME
capability: Multilingual European legal classification and named-entity recognition across 24 languages.

source: European legislation, cases, and legal NLP datasets
input: Legal text or token sequence

verified: Paper defines 11 datasets, 24 languages, macro-F1, and hierarchical harmonic aggregation.

name: FairLex
capability: Evaluate legal prediction performance and group robustness across sensitive or legally salient subpopulations.

source: Court decisions with gender, age, region, language, and legal-area attributes where available

verified: Official paper/repository cover four jurisdictions and five languages with group-robustness metrics.

name: Atticus Clause Retrieval Dataset
capability: Rank precedent contract clauses for an attorney-written drafting need.

reproducibility: High with official BEIR files and qrels; HF viewer currently mis-parses the zip, so use raw files.
